meta.title: Rapid 3D Bioprinting of Glioblastoma Model Mimicking Native Biophysical Heterogeneity.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Light-based (DLP) printing built glioblastoma models with patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells and endothelial cells in GelMA/hyaluronic acid matrices of tumour-like (7 kPa) and brain-like (0.45 kPa) stiffness.

formulations.stiffness_note: tumour core designed to match GBM tissue; brain region 0.45 kPa
formulations.name: GelMA + methacrylated hyaluronic acid (stiff tumour core)
formulations.composition_detail: GelMA and GMHA blends tuned to 7 kPa (tumour) and 0.45 kPa (brain)
formulations.key_outcome: Stiff tumour regions and soft brain regions in one print reproduced GBM's biophysical heterogeneity.

evidence.quote: Matrix stiffness of the tumor core and the endothelial regions was designed to mimic that of GBM patient tissues (7 kPa) and normal brain tissues (0.45 kPa).
Flexibility of the DLP-based bioprinting process and versatile material selection allow orthogonal modulation of biophysical properties and biochemical characteristics.
